Yes, I saw this also. "address" was added to restore the old "platform" behavior, but to my mind that was a mistake.

comments.body:
Thank you for the quick reply! 

I tried to use `os.environ["XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR"] = "address"` now, but it is not in the available options. I get the following for both `0.10.1` and `0.10.2`.
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/yigit/anaconda3/envs/gpu-jax-101/lib/python3.13/site-packages/jax/_src/xla_bridge.py", line 495, in discover_pjrt_plugins
    plugin_module.initialize()
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/home/yigit/anaconda3/envs/gpu-jax-101/lib/python3.13/site-packages/jax_plugins/xla_cuda12/__init__.py", line 372, in initialize
    options = xla_client.generate_pjrt_gpu_plugin_options()
  File "/home/yigit/anaconda3/envs/gpu-jax-101/lib/python3.13/site-packages/jaxlib/xla_client.py", line 194, in generate_pjrt_gpu_plugin_options
    raise ValueError(
    ...<2 lines>...
    )
ValueError: XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR env var must be "default", "platform", "bfc", "cuda_async", or "vmm", got "address"
```

I know `address` is experimental for now, but I wanted to share the behavior here.
